messages:
Elena: Ran a perfetto + nvprof pass on release/opt-1.3 using the production seq-dist. Attaching quick summary — can we pick top 2 kernels to tackle first?
Matt: Saw the dump, looks like total-GPU-time is dominated by fused_attention_forward. SM util is low during small_gemm spikes :thinking:
Jia: Confirmed. KV cache thrash + shortest sequences cause many tiny GEMMs. Timeline excerpt:
```
0.117s fused_attention_forward 48.1ms
0.165s small_gemm_32x128 13.9ms (lots of launches)
0.189s kv_cache_apply 9.4ms
0.205s small_gemm_32x64 7.1ms
```
perf-bot: Profile summary: top kernels by aggregate time: fused_attention_forward 44.6%, small_gemm_32x128 16.2%, kv_cache_apply 11.3%, small_gemm_32x64 7.8%.
Rob: Two vectors: optimize fused_attention (kernel fusion/tiling) and reduce overhead from tiny GEMMs (coalesce launches or batched microkernels). Also check occupancy: fused_attention has low achieved occupancy on A100 40GB config.
Anya: Also worth trying a micro-batching window for short sequences (e.g. 6–10ms wait) to merge tiny requests; increases tail latency slightly but reduces overall token cost.
Matt: Can we reproduce with perf/trace harness? Jia — can you throw a deterministic KV access pattern into the harness and gdb/profile?
Jia: On it. I'll push a trace config and a minimal repro. Will add nvprof and a perfetto timeline with kernel names and SM util heatmap.
Elena: Great — once we have deterministic trace, we'll rank hotspots and open a perf plan. I'm going to create a ticket and assign Jia + Rob. Thanks :thumbsup:
